knowledge_point.title: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-7 & 5 & -2 \\ 7 & 6 & -9 \\ -4 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}$ on $M?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-7 & 5 & -2 \\ 7 & 6 & -9 \\ -4 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}7 & 6 & -9 \\ -7 & 5 & -2 \\ -4 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -7 & -5 & -7 \\ -1 & 3 & -6 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{1}:=-7R_{1}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{1}:=-7R_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $-7.$

Multiplying the $1$st row by $-7$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -7 & -5 & -7 \\ -1 & 3 & -6 & -7\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}:=-7R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-7\cdot 3 & -7\cdot 2 & -7\cdot (-2) & -7\cdot (-1) \\ 1 & -7 & -5 & -7 \\ -1 & 3 & -6 & -7\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-21 & -14 & 14 & 7 \\ 1 & -7 & -5 & -7 \\ -1 & 3 & -6 & -7\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}9 & 0 & 8 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & -7 & -1 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{1}:=R_{1}+(-3)\cdot R_{3}$ on $N?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{1}:=R_{1}+(-3)\cdot R_{3}$ means that we need to add $-3$ times the third row to the first row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
N=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}9 & 0 & 8 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & -7 & -1 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}:=R_{1}+(-3)\cdot R_{3}
$$

$$
\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}9+(-3)(3) & 0+(-3)(-6) & 8+(-3)(-7) & 1+(-3)(-4) \\ -7 & -5 & -7 & -1 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4\end{array}\right]}
$$

$$
\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}0 & 18 & 29 & 13 \\ -7 & -5 & -7 & -1 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-6 & 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 5 & -9 & -3 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & 5 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}R_{1} &\leftrightarrow R_{2} \\ R_{2} &:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation $R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

- The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-6 & 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 5 & -9 & -3 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & 5 & 4\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}5 & -9 & -3 & -3 \\ -6 & 2 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -6 & 5 & 4\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1} \\ &\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}5 & -9 & -3 & -3 \\ -6+(-1)(5) & 2+(-1)(-9) & 5+(-1)(-3) & 2+(-1)(-3) \\ -3 & -6 & 5 & 4\end{array}\right]} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}5 & -9 & -3 & -3 \\ -11 & 11 & 8 & 5 \\ -3 & -6 & 5 & 4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-6 & 6 & 2 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4 \\ 2 & -9 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $N?$

$$
\begin{aligned}R_{1} &:=-2R_{1} \\ R_{3} &:=R_{3}+(3)\cdot R_{1}\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation $R_{1}:=-2R_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $-2.$

- The operation $R_{3}:=R_{3}+(3)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}N &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-6 & 6 & 2 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4 \\ 2 & -9 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}:=-2R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}12 & -12 & -4 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4 \\ 2 & -9 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]\,R_{3}:=R_{3}+(3)\cdot R_{1} \\ &\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}12 & -12 & -4 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4 \\ 2+(3)(12) & -9+(3)(-12) & -1+(3)(-4) & 0+(3)(4)\end{array}\right]} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}12 & -12 & -4 & 4 \\ 3 & -6 & -7 & -4 \\ 38 & -45 & -13 & 12\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$
